rounds.text: Jigar Cables Ltd is presenting a compelling valuation case supported by intrinsic value models, where a discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at Rs 81 per share compared to the market price of Rs 65, offering a margin of safety of 19.7% [E39, E40]. Furthermore, a reverse DCF indicates that the current price implies an earnings growth rate of only 14.9%, which sits below the base case assumption of 18.0% [E41]. Long-term compounding metrics highlight strong fundamental growth, with 5-year compounded sales growth at 32% and profit growth at 34%, alongside 3-year compounded sales growth at 27% and profit growth at 20% [E14, E15, E17, E18]. Recent operational performance shows positive momentum, evidenced by quarterly operating margins increasing over the last 4 quarters and expanding by 2 percentage points year-over-year in Mar 2026 to 6%, while debtor days have notably improved from 40.1 to 19.6 days [E27, E29, E45]. Balance sheet stability is supported by a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 2.86x and moderate leverage with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.39x as of Mar 2026 [E33, E34]. Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow are negative at Rs -1.43 Cr and Rs -16.24 Cr respectively, alongside a low 3-year median return on equity of 7% [E24, E31, E32].

Despite a benign macro backdrop, Jigar Cables Ltd carries significant structural and financial risks that undermine its current valuation. The company trades at an elevated P/E of 32.5x, which represents a clear premium over the sector benchmark of 21.3x [E1, E6]. This rich multiple is difficult to justify given that key profitability metrics lag behind industry peers, with an ROE of 7.02% and ROCE of 8.54% compared to sector benchmarks of 10.88% and 12.96% respectively [E9, E10]. Furthermore, the business has experienced a severe top-line contraction recently, evidenced by a compounded sales growth rate of -45% over the trailing twelve months [E16]. Underneath the reported earnings lie troubling cash flow dynamics, as operating cash flow turned negative to Rs -1.43 Cr alongside a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.79x and a staggering negative free cash flow of Rs -16.24 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30, E31, E32]. This cash drain is accompanied by a sharp escalation in debt, with borrowings jumping more than fourfold from Rs 2.83 Cr to Rs 11.93 Cr year-over-year, while potential red flags suggest the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E35, E48]. Insider alignment is also slowly eroding, with promoter shareholding ticking down from 44.48% to 42.48% [E37], and shareholders receive zero return on their capital via dividends [E4]. Conceded: the company boasts a five-year compounded sales growth of 32% and a discounted cash flow intrinsic value estimate above the current market price [E14, E39].

Conceded: trailing twelve months sales growth is negative [E16], borrowings rose to Rs 11.93 Cr [E35], and promoter holding ticked down slightly [E37]. However, the bear's valuation critique ignores that the price-to-book ratio of 1.78x trades at a clear discount to the sector benchmark of 2.39x [E7]. Furthermore, the fundamental growth record remains robust over multi-year horizons, with a 5-year compounded sales growth of 32% and a 5-year profit growth of 34% [E14, E17]. Results are actively improving with net profit up 78% year-over-year and quarterly operating margins expanding to 6% from 4% in the year-ago quarter [E27, E52, E57]. The discount cash flow model explicitly places intrinsic value at Rs 81 against the market price of Rs 65, providing a 19.7% margin of safety [E39, E40], and a reverse DCF demonstrates that the current price assumes less growth than the base case actually requires [E41]. Finally, debtor days have significantly improved from 40.1 to 19.6 days [E45] and short-term liquidity is comfortable with a current ratio of 2.86x [E34].

Conceded: price-to-book of 1.78x sits below the sector benchmark of 2.39x [E7], and intrinsic value is estimated at Rs 81 against the market price of Rs 65 [E39]. However, that relative book discount and DCF output must be weighed against severe operational deterioration: trailing twelve months sales have plummeted by 45% [E16], and profit growth over the same TTM period flatlined at -1% [E19]. While the bull highlights margin expansion and 78% YoY profit growth [E27, E52], this short-term bounce occurs against a backdrop of chronically depressed efficiency, evidenced by a stagnant 7% median return on equity over 3 and 5 years [E23, E24] that lags the sector benchmark of 10.88% [E9]. Furthermore, the bull's emphasis on strong short-term liquidity and improving debtor days [E34, E45] completely ignores the catastrophic cash burn where operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 1.43 Cr and free cash flow plummeted to negative Rs 16.24 Cr [E31, E32], leading to a dismal cash conversion ratio of -0.79x [E30]. Finally, this cash drain has forced borrowings to spike fourfold to Rs 11.93 Cr [E35], while suspicions linger that the company may even be capitalizing its interest costs [E48].
